newsitem.title: USA: Three teams to battle for new U.S. warship.
newsitem.headline: Three teams to battle for new U.S. warship.

text.p: The Pentagon on Friday picked three industry teams headed by Lockheed Martin Corp., Northrop Grumman Corp. and General Dynamics Corp. to compete in designing a new "Arsenal Ship" that could change naval warfare in five years.

The three teams, narrowed from a field of five, each won a $15 million contract to work for one year on proposals for the missile-packed stealth warship. One team will be chosen next year to build a prototype of the vessel.
Final work on the proposed fleet of six ships could be worth more than $3 billion to the eventual winner. Tentative plans are to launch the first ship in 2001.

Teams headed by the Hughes Aircraft Co. division of General Motors Corp. and by Rockwell International Corp. which had been among five named last year to work on the ship, were dropped as the field was narrowed on Friday.

With U.S. military budgets and forces shrinking after the Cold War, the Pentagon has asked defence contractors to compete in designing a sleek and almost unsinkable Navy ship packed with 500 missile launchers and space age communications.

Expected to cost $550 million each, a bargain at today's prices, each of the six ships would be manned by fewer than 50 sailors -- or perhaps no crew at all as they evolve -- with missiles and artillery that might even be triggered by Army officers ashore.
In contrast, the Navy's huge aircraft carriers carry a crew of 5,000 each and cost $1 million a day to operate.

The new multi-hull weapons platform, which the Pentagon plans to develop aggressively and test in only five years compared to 15 normally needed for new ships, could lay near world hotspots and maintain peace through U.S. intimidation.
The Pentagon has budgeted $520 million for research over the next four years.

Dimensions of the Arsenal Ship have not even been determined, but Navy and private experts say it has wide support in the military because it would support land and other forces with a variety of missiles to destroy tanks, aircraft and other ships.

In addition to a sleek and low provile that would make it hard to spot on radar, the ship would include composite materials to absorb radar signals and would also have at least two hulls to protect its insides from explosive damage.

Its weapons would include 700-mile (1,127-km) range Tomahawk cruise missiles, and there are tentative plans to arm the ship with vertical 155mm artillery guns below decks that could fire pinpoint tank-destroying shells more than 250 miles (400 km).
